Precondition:
1) BASE device configuration
2) SSG scheduler enabled
3) Boost control available at /dev/blkio/background/blkio.ssg.boost_on
4) Same test file and workload used for both runs
Test scenario:
1) Run foreground random read, 4K, QD1 with boost OFF
2) Repeat with boost ON
3) Run foreground random write, 4K, QD1 with boost OFF and ON
4) Repeat each test at least 5 times
Implementation steps:
1) Set boost to 0 and verify state
2) Run fio and collect performance
3) Set boost to 1 and verify state
4) Add test PID to appropriate boost cgroup, as required
5) Repeat identical fio workload
6) Compare results
Suggested configuration: Random read/write, 4K block size, QD1, fixed test size and runtime. Keep fio parameters identical in both conditions
Metrics: IOPS, bandwidth, average latency, p95 latency, p99 latency, CPU utilisation
Expected result:
1) Boost ON should improve foreground I/O performance compared with OFF
2) Latency should reduce, particularly at p95/p99
3) Results should be repeatable across runs
Feasibility explanation / dependencies: Requires a working boost control, correct cgroup assignment and a repeatable fio workload
Does this test check the SSG scheduler?: Yes — checks whether enabling SSG boost changes foreground I/O scheduling behaviour
What this test proves: Whether boost provides a measurable performance benefit instead of merely changing its control state
Remark: Use the same workload, device condition and thermal state for ON/OFF comparisons

Precondition:
1) BASE configuration
2) SSG scheduler enabled
3) Foreground and background cgroups available
4) Boost control working
Test scenario:
1) Run background sequential write, 1M, QD32
2) Simultaneously run foreground random read, 4K, QD1
3) Repeat with boost OFF and ON
4) Repeat with foreground random write, 4K, QD1
Implementation steps:
1) Start background fio workload
2) Start foreground fio workload
3) Record foreground and background performance with boost OFF
4) Enable boost and assign foreground PID to appropriate cgroup
5) Repeat same workload
6) Compare foreground latency and background bandwidth
Suggested configuration:
FG: random read/write, 4K, QD1
BG: sequential write, 1M, QD32
Use separate fio processes
Metrics: FG p50/p95/p99 latency, FG IOPS, BG bandwidth, BG completion time, CPU utilisation
Expected result:
1) Foreground latency should improve with boost ON
2) Background workload should continue making progress
3) Background throughput reduction should remain within an agreed limit
Feasibility explanation / dependencies: Requires concurrent fio workloads and correct foreground/background cgroup assignment
Does this test check the SSG scheduler?: Yes — checks how SSG prioritises boosted I/O under contention
What this test proves: Whether boost makes interactive foreground operations faster while background I/O is running
Remark: Check background starvation as well as foreground improvement

Precondition:
1) BASE configuration
2) SSG scheduler enabled
3) Boost control accessible
4) I/O workload running continuously
Test scenario:
1) Run continuous foreground random read, 4K, QD1
2) Toggle boost OFF → ON → OFF while workload is running
3) Repeat sequence 20 times
4) Record performance around every transition
Implementation steps:
1) Start fio and capture timestamped logs
2) Enable boost
3) Record time until performance changes
4) Disable boost
5) Record time until performance returns towards normal
6) Repeat 20 times
Suggested configuration: Random read, 4K, QD1; continuous workload; boost ON/OFF transitions at fixed intervals
Metrics: Boost transition time, IOPS, bandwidth, p99 latency, transition-related latency spikes, failed transitions
Expected result:
1) Boost should take effect consistently after activation
2) Performance should return towards normal after deactivation
3) No unexpected I/O stalls or errors during transitions
Feasibility explanation / dependencies: Requires timestamped logging and reliable boost toggling while fio is active. Define transition-time limits from implementation
Does this test check the SSG scheduler?: Yes — checks scheduler response to boost state changes
What this test proves: Whether boost reacts reliably when an application starts or stops needing priority
Remark: Verify actual boost state after each write; a successful shell command alone does not prove scheduler application

Precondition:
1) BASE configuration
2) SSG scheduler enabled
3) Boost control and required cgroups available
4) Test applications installed
Test scenario:
1) Run background download or large file write
2) Launch application while background I/O is active
3) Measure launch time with boost OFF
4) Repeat with boost ON
5) Perform 10 cold launches per condition
Implementation steps:
1) Prepare same application and conditions
2) Start background I/O
3) Launch application and record launch time
4) Repeat with boost enabled and foreground PID assigned to boost cgroup
5) Compare median and p90 launch times
Suggested configuration: Background sequential write or download; foreground application launch; 10 cold launches per condition
Metrics: Application launch time, median, p90, p99 where available, foreground read latency, background write bandwidth, frame drops
Expected result:
1) Boost ON should improve or maintain application launch time
2) No additional UI stuttering
3) Background I/O should continue without indefinite starvation
Feasibility explanation / dependencies: Requires Android test application, repeatable launch procedure, PID tracking and reliable boost activation. Launch time is also affected by CPU, memory and cache state
Does this test check the SSG scheduler?: Yes — checks whether boost improves storage responsiveness during a real application launch
What this test proves: Whether boost provides a user-visible benefit rather than only improving synthetic fio numbers
Remark: Control app cache state, background activity and thermal conditions between runs

Precondition:
1) BASE configuration
2) SSG scheduler enabled
3) Foreground and background cgroups available
4) Boost state controllable
Test scenario:
1) Run one boosted foreground random read workload
2) Run two background random read/write workloads simultaneously
3) Maintain workload for 30 minutes
4) Compare boost ON and OFF
Implementation steps:
1) Start both background fio processes
2) Start foreground fio process
3) Enable boost for foreground process
4) Record performance at regular intervals
5) Repeat with boost OFF
6) Compare foreground latency, background throughput and variation
Suggested configuration:
FG: random read, 4K, QD1
BG1/BG2: random read/write, 4K, QD32 each
Run for 30 minutes
Metrics: FG p95/p99 latency, BG1/BG2 IOPS, BG bandwidth, throughput share, latency variation, CPU utilisation, I/O stalls
Expected result:
1) Boosted foreground latency should remain controlled
2) Both background jobs should continue progressing
3) No prolonged starvation
4) No unexpected performance degradation over 30 minutes
Feasibility explanation / dependencies: Requires three concurrent workloads, separate process tracking and stable thermal environment
Does this test check the SSG scheduler?: Yes — evaluates boost priority, fairness and long-duration scheduling behaviour
What this test proves: Whether boost prioritises important I/O without starving other applications or becoming unstable during prolonged use
Remark: Check background job shares and starvation; do not assume equal throughput unless workloads and priorities are equivalent
